builds.name: Reference: Ranked top core
builds.goal: Reference for Garen: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ top players use most (11,036 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 55.1% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A durable melee finisher who clears slows, silences a target and spins in contact before using missing-health execution. The current top provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Stridebreaker → Phantom Dancer → Mortal Reminder. Conqueror keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Berserker's Greaves, Dead Man's Plate, Sterak's Gage.
builds.summary: The proven top baseline: Stridebreaker → Phantom Dancer → Mortal Reminder, with Conqueror.
testPlan: Play it in top as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Stridebreaker → Phantom Dancer → Mortal Reminder) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 55.1% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Stridebreaker → Phantom Dancer → Mortal Reminder.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

builds.name: Nearest Spin Shred
builds.summary: Compare early and post-six-strike E packets with a nearby decoy unit.
builds.goal: Compare early and post-six-strike E packets with a nearby decoy unit.
builds.hypothesis: E increases damage to the nearest enemy and shreds armor after six strikes. Stridebreaker access and Cleaver physical shred may help the later spins; Shojin tests ability/passive amplification and AD investment without assuming every E strike is an attack on-hit.
testPlan: Required state: Stay the nearest unit to the intended target and land at least six E strikes.
Compare early and post-six-strike E packets with a nearby decoy unit; repeat at equal gold, finite stacks, same ranks and defenses against a moving target.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: A nearer minion redirects bonus damage or the target exits before shred.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Nashor/Rageblade on-hits are not automatically applied per spin.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Stridebreaker, Black Cleaver, Spear of Shojin, Sterak's Gage, Death's Dance, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Q evidence: Garen gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him. His next attack strikes a vital area of his foe, dealing bonus damage and silencing them. builds.name: Perseverance Reset Duel
builds.summary: Measure second-entry health and Q trade after a controlled eight-second reset.
builds.goal: Measure second-entry health and Q trade after a controlled eight-second reset.
builds.hypothesis: P heals a percentage of max health after eight seconds without qualifying damage. Q removes slows and gives movement for disengage; earned Heartsteel health and W's health shield support a second entry. Trinity rewards Q's actual attack and Randuin helps control the exit/return.
testPlan: Required state: Record earned health, W unit stacks and an eight-second safe break.
Measure second-entry health and Q trade after a controlled eight-second reset; repeat at equal gold, finite stacks, same ranks and defenses against a moving target.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: DoT/chip resets recovery or disengage surrenders the objective.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: In-combat waiting does not enable Perseverance.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
